live.body:
## Question

For literal-only Find, what precise matching and asynchronous evaluation contract will implement the remaining reviewed design?

## Current scope

Confirmed with the maintainer on 2026-10-26: regular-expression search is out of scope for this effort. Omit the `.*` mode control. Keep Match case and Whole words. Treat regex punctuation as ordinary query text. This supersedes regex-specific requirements and three-mode references in the reviewed draft and earlier decision comments; the remaining product and state/identity contracts still apply.

Do not select a user-pattern dialect, regex flags, invalid-pattern/zero-width behavior, or catastrophic-pattern deadlines as part of this decision. Completed regex experiments remain historical evidence. They do not require a utility process or any other execution mechanism for the literal-only scope. Internal implementation techniques for literal matching remain an engineering choice; this scope boundary concerns user-supplied pattern syntax.

## Decision to resolve

Resolve through live grilling plus domain-modeling: the execution mechanism and any packaging seam actually needed for literal matching; Unicode case and whole-word behavior; record-level results, original-string occurrence ranges and application-text/decoded-message provenance; obsolete-work cancellation, startup/disposal and lifetime; measured literal-workload budgets and user feedback. Preserve exact record counts/navigation even when display-decoration work is separately bounded. Do not substitute a regex experiment's timeout for a measured literal-search target.

Define the request/result identity needed to reject obsolete target/container-instance, query/mode, snapshot and extracted-message revisions, while allowing valid count updates without resurrecting an origin or reveal. Query/mode identity now covers literal text, Match case and Whole words only. Coordinate the protocol with the state/identity decision; document any real incompatibility with the remaining reviewed behavior rather than silently changing it.

The resolution must provide concrete interfaces/invariants, chosen values with evidence, and the regressions needed to implement this contract. It is a technical decision and acceptance specification, not the production matching implementation.

Related decisions and evidence: [Establish packaged Find execution and Unicode matching facts](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/34); [Measure Find evaluation at retained-window limits](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/35); [Define Find state, reading anchors and occurrence identity](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/37); [Validate text-safe highlights, hidden matches and scrollbar marks](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/38).

comments.body:
## Scope update and partial agreement

The maintainer explicitly deferred regular-expression search during the live Wayfinder discussion on 2026-10-26 and requested that the map reflect it. This effort now covers literal-only Find, retaining Match case and Whole words. The regex mode/control and regex-specific decisions and acceptance gates are out of scope for now; completed experiments remain historical evidence. The parent map and remaining decision tickets have been updated accordingly.

The maintainer also agreed to non-overlapping occurrence enumeration: `ana` in `banana` highlights the first `ana`, and that record counts once. This is a partial agreement, not the resolution of this ticket. Execution mechanism, literal case-folding policy and numeric budgets remain open; the earlier utility-process recommendation was not accepted by this scope change.

## Partial agreement: literal Unicode semantics and execution

The maintainer answered “yes to all” to the following two recommendations in the live Wayfinder discussion on 2026-10-26:

- Use locale-independent Unicode simple/common case folding for case-insensitive literal Find. For example, `K` matches `k` and `K`, and Greek `σ` matches `ς`; `SS` does not match `ß`. Do not remove accents, normalize character sequences, or apply locale-specific casing. Composed `é` remains distinct from `e` plus a combining accent. Match case requires exact characters. Preserve original-string UTF-16 offsets and the previously agreed Unicode whole-word rule.
- Use a reusable background Node worker owned by the Freelens main extension, through the already demonstrated extension-scoped SDK messaging seam. The separate utility-process candidate is not selected. The existing actual-host evidence establishes feasibility and cleanup, not final production budgets.

This builds on the already recorded literal-only scope and left-to-right non-overlapping text matches. User regex syntax and the `.*` control remain out of scope.

This is **partial agreement**, not the final resolution. Numeric input/output/time budgets, latest-work scheduling and cancellation, worker lifetime/failure policy, and the concrete request/result protocol remain to settle. Long Unicode, dense Whole words rejection and long literal-query measurements are still needed before treating proposed numeric limits as measured targets. The ticket remains open and claimed.

## Partial agreement: worker lifetime, replacement and failure recovery

The maintainer answered “agree with all” to the next live Wayfinder round on 2026-10-26:

- **Lifetime:** create one main-owned worker for an active viewer when its first nonempty search needs evaluation; reuse it and release it when that viewer becomes inactive or closes. Temporary inactivity preserves query, modes, history and surviving occurrence-based state. Closing only Find or opening Profiles preserves that state and may keep matching current while the viewer stays active; canceled selection/reveal intents never replay. Release all owned execution on extension deactivation or app shutdown.
- **Replacement:** invalidate obsolete matching results immediately, cancel obsolete running work, and retain at most the newest replacement for that viewer while the previous worker exits. No backlog of queries or old navigation actions. The complete input key and independent selection/reveal validity remain governed by [Define Find state, reading anchors and occurrence identity](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/37#issuecomment-6408002921).
- **Failure:** stop with local Find feedback; leave logs available and the query editable. Recover on an explicit edit or Retry action, without an automatic retry loop or a silent change of execution mechanism. Internal literal-matcher failures are not user regex-syntax errors.

The [new immutable literal-workload report](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/blob/d53e2c91d6cd267e1eaced5fd027653fd893e041/docs/research/find-literal-budgets.md), [raw samples](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/blob/d53e2c91d6cd267e1eaced5fd027653fd893e041/docs/research/find-literal-budgets/raw.json) and [reproducible script](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/blob/d53e2c91d6cd267e1eaced5fd027653fd893e041/scripts/find-literal-budgets/measure.mjs) are pushed on `research/find-literal-budgets` at `d53e2c91d6cd267e1eaced5fd027653fd893e041`, with no PR or merge.

The headless installed-Electron/Node-worker matrix includes all four literal mode combinations, actual 1,000-record / 5 MiB retention inputs, long Unicode, dense whole-word rejection, duplicated fallback-message sources and long punctuation-rich literal queries. Across 416 measured outcomes: 368 correct completions, 48 preserved internal matcher failures on 65,536-unit queries, no deadlines; maximum caller elapsed 12.11 ms. All tested 16,384-unit cases complete. Fresh startup maximum is 17.18 ms. All 16 fresh-worker recoveries pass and no owned worker remains. These are Linux small-sample observations, not mounted renderer/IPC, DOM, native-input, cross-platform or long-term resource acceptance.

This remains **partial agreement**. Query/time/range budgets and the final concrete protocol are not yet resolved. The report's 100 ms / 1,000 ms / 16,384-unit / 4,096-range values are candidates until the maintainer accepts them.

## Question

What explicit viewer state, events and occurrence references will implement the reviewed reading-row, query-refinement and lifecycle behavior without conflating inspection, text selection, keyboard focus and the active Find result?

Resolve through live grilling plus domain-modeling using concrete event sequences from the design. Specify reading row, search origin, active result, last successful refinement candidate, current search position and pending reveal; deliberate activation versus focus restoration; inclusive initial seeks versus strict navigation; whole-input replacement using pre-insertion selection; composition/paste/undo/clear/history/selected-text input; mode changes; temporary no-match edits; history commitment; opener/popover focus and one-layer dismissal.

Reconcile the current inspection text-plus-occurrence-from-end selection with the ordered-overlap references used by Find/viewport. Decide how one observed occurrence survives snapshot replacement, duplicate lines and eviction without promising identity the retention model cannot observe. Specify target/container-instance epochs and reset signals, including restart with the same selected container. Define reveal cancellation and what pending results may update after origin/inspection changes. Preserve ordinary following and explicit Pause.

The resolution must give a state/event table or equivalent concise model, clear ownership at the existing module boundaries, and acceptance traces covering races and duplicates. It must integrate with the asynchronous matching contract; do not implement the production reducer/controller here.

Related decisions and evidence: [Choose Find matching semantics and resource budgets](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/36); [Agree the Find implementation plan and acceptance gates](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/39).

comments.body:
## Resolution: Find state, reading anchors and occurrence identity

The maintainer confirmed the behavior choices below through live grilling. This is an implementation contract, not a production implementation or a claim of packaged/native verification. The reviewed [Find final design draft](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/blob/a774370c71193b4e3603bab9eee83189fb38c67b/docs/design/search-final-design.md) remains the product reference.

### One observed occurrence, independent user states

Adopt one shared occurrence mapping for inspection, the reading row, Find, and viewport retention. Use the existing longest exact old-suffix/new-prefix overlap of complete transport lines. Assign opaque occurrence IDs to newly observed entries; carry IDs only through that overlap. References contain a live viewer/target/instance context and an occurrence ID. A numeric row index, matching text, or an occurrence counted backward from the end is not a cross-snapshot reference.

- `[start, x, end] → [x, end, x]` retains the old `x` at new index 0. Inspection must not switch to the newly appended `x` at index 2.
- Zero overlap expires all old references. Identical windows preserve the same observed mapping. Neither case authorizes a text-search fallback or a claim to detect unseen identical additions.
- On expiry, close an inspector whose record disappeared and clear a reading anchor referring to that occurrence. Clear an expired Find result, give local expired-result feedback, and keep the query without selecting a substitute. If the inspector and reading row refer to different occurrences, expiry/closure of the inspector preserves the separate reading row.
- Give row DOM identity the same occurrence basis; do not key retained rows by transient indices. Preserving actual browser selection/focus across presentation updates still needs rendering evidence; an occurrence ID alone does not establish that behavior.

The current conflict is source-verified: [ordered-overlap navigation](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/blob/c0f73384c13a2bc0b0eb0ecfa1f48d9b0b324528/src/core/navigation.ts#L3-L28) and [inspection's occurrence-from-end selection](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/blob/c0f73384c13a2bc0b0eb0ecfa1f48d9b0b324528/src/core/inspection.ts#L4-L22) currently disagree in the duplicate example. Unify the seam; do not merge/deduplicate records or change retention/acquisition.

### State and ownership

The viewer owns the following independent states. Pure helpers calculate occurrence mapping and seeks; the viewport consumes validated reveal intents and owns geometry/following.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Context | Viewer lifetime, target identity including Pod UID, and observed container-instance epoch. |
| Window/message revisions | The immutable retained occurrences and extracted-message inputs being evaluated. Presentation-only changes do not create a new search scope. |
| Reading row | A deliberate user-chosen occurrence used for a new query or initial navigation. It need not be inspected. |
| Inspection | Its own occurrence, content tab and layout. Opening it does not inherently choose a reading row. |
| Query/edit sequence | Exact text, the three mode flags, query revision, edit-sequence identity and composition transaction. |
| Search origin | The record or window edge selected as the base of the current seek. It is captured per intent, not a permanently fixed original row. |
| Search position | The last successful search position, initially the chosen reading row or a window-edge sentinel. Retain it across a temporary no-match edit while its occurrence survives. |
| Active Find result | The currently addressed occurrence, validated against the current matching result. Its ordinal is derived from the current matching-record order. |
| Refinement candidate | The latest successful result retained through temporary no-match/error edits. It is not displayed as a current hit when it does not match. |
| Evaluation | The current logical input key, pending/ready/no-match/invalid/timed-out status, ordered matching occurrences and range/provenance data. Never display an old count as a completed count for new inputs. |
| Selection/reveal intents | Separate permissions to choose a result and scroll to it. Completing an evaluation does not itself grant either permission. |
| Find UI | Open/closed, valid opener/focus return target, history popover, status feedback and up to seven committed query/mode entries. |

Browser text selection, DOM focus, ordinary viewport following and explicit Pause remain independent. Do not infer a reading row from hover, scroll position, native Lens selection, or a generic focus event.

### State/event contract

| Event | Transition and effect |
| --- | --- |
| Deliberately focus a row through real keyboard navigation | Set that reading row without opening inspection; clear active result and refinement candidate, rebase search position, cancel older selection/reveal intents. Keep query/count. Do not add new row-navigation shortcuts as part of this decision. |
| Activate a row by an ordinary click or existing Enter/Space action | Select/inspect it and apply the same reading-row rebase. A click that deselects the already inspected row closes inspection and clears the anchor belonging to that row. Preserve any independently chosen reading row. Drag selection/multi-click selection does not activate a row. |
| Close inspection | Clear its reading anchor only if the anchor still refers to the inspected occurrence. Preserve an independently established active Find result and refinement candidate when valid. Cancel older selection/reveal intents. Restore focus without creating an anchor. |
| Inspect a hidden-match explanation | Open the relevant occurrence and representation tab; preserve the reading row, active Find result and search position. This is not row activation or a new search. |
| Start a new nonempty query | Start a new edit sequence; discard the previous query's active result/candidate/position. Seek forward inclusively from the current reading row, otherwise the beginning of all retained logs. Scrolling does not change this base. |
| Refine text or toggle a matching mode | Keep a matching candidate. Otherwise seek forward inclusively from the latest surviving search position. A successful seek updates active result, candidate and position; zero matches clears only the active result and keeps the surviving candidate/position for correction. Never advance solely because another character was typed. |
| Explicit Up/Down, Enter/Shift+Enter, local repeat shortcut | With an active result, seek strictly previous/next. Without one, seek inclusively from the reading row, otherwise Up uses the last match and Down the first. Wrap with the reviewed feedback; one hit stays active with `Only matching record`. Keep/focus Find input without selecting its text on every navigation. |
| Activate a scrollbar match mark | Address exactly that matching occurrence, update candidate/position, request its reveal and focus Find. Do not inspect or choose a reading row. Commit history as explicit Find navigation. |
| Clear or edit to empty | End the edit sequence; clear query, active result, candidate, search position/origin, decorations, feedback and pending intents. Keep reading row, inspection, scroll, history and mode flags. The clear button keeps Find open and focused. |
| Open Find | Capture eligible text selection and reading context before moving focus. If empty, a valid selection seeds the query. Otherwise keep the query. Focus/select the retained input text; opening alone does not navigate or reveal. |
| Close Find | Commit an eligible query, hide Find/popover, preserve query/modes and surviving references; cancel pending selection/reveal intents. Restore its valid opener, with viewport fallback. No implicit following/Pause change. |
| Enter Profiles or temporarily deactivate this viewer | Preserve temporary search state while valid; cancel pending selection/reveal intents and suspend local shortcut ownership. Background input changes may update matching state without scrolling. Return does not run a new search or restore an old jump. |
| Manually scroll while evaluation/reveal is pending | Cancel the older reveal permission. A current evaluation may still update matching state and an otherwise live selection intent, but cannot undo the user's scroll. A new explicit edit/navigation can create a new reveal permission. |
| Accept a replacement snapshot | Map every occurrence reference once through the shared overlap, expiring missing references. Cancel old evaluation/reveal work; evaluate current inputs in maintenance mode. Preserve a surviving active result only if it still matches. New matches, including the first matches for a previously empty result set, update counts without choosing/revealing a result. |
| Change formatting profile/extracted message | Re-evaluate without fetching. Preserve a result that still matches; otherwise clear it without automatically choosing another. Cancel obsolete evaluation/reveal intents. Keep valid inspection and reading occurrence references. |
| Change Raw/Readable, wrap, timestamps or inspection layout | Preserve query, modes and occurrence references. Recompute presentation/geometry as required; never change the matching scope or start a search. Reject stale geometry before executing a still-live explicit reveal. |
| Target/container/observed instance changes or teardown | Invalidate context and all pending work; reset query, modes, history, origins, candidates and results, and clear old occurrence references. Returning to the same target name is still a new context. |

The row-focus boundary must track actual input intent. Programmatic focus restoration, finding/revealing a record, pointer focus during a drag and focus returning from an inspector must not dispatch a deliberate row-focus event. Use existing IME/AltGraph/shortcut guards for row commands too. Closing an inspector restores focus after state invalidation, so focus cannot recreate the cleared anchor.

### Input transactions, history and dismissal

- Detect whole-input replacement from the nonempty input's selection **before insertion**. Full replacement by typing/paste is a new sequence even when old/new strings share a prefix; partial insertion/paste/deletion refines. Deleting/cutting the entire value ends the sequence. Do not trim query text or infer replacement from prefix comparison.
- Capture that pre-edit decision before composition begins. Native composing text may update in the input, but invalidate old pending intents and do not match or navigate until composition commits. Evaluate the final committed text once, respecting whether composition replaced the whole input. Suppress duplicate composition-end/input evaluation and late composition completion after clear/disposal. Preserve native caret, selection, paste and undo behavior; no idle timer changes edit meaning.
- Undo/Redo is refinement, without a search-position undo history. Crossing through an empty value ends the sequence; the next nonempty value starts from the current reading row or beginning.
- Seed only an empty input from a single-line selection of actual log text within one record or its inspector, at most 256 Unicode code points. Ignore foreign/multi-record/generated-label selections. Seeding supplies exact query text and preserves current mode flags; it does not choose the source record as the reading row. Do not replace an existing query.
- History entries are exact nonempty text plus all three mode flags, distinct by that tuple, MRU, maximum seven, memory-only per viewer/context. Commit on enabled explicit navigation or Close Find, including Escape closing Find. Include completed valid zero-hit queries when closing; exclude invalid, timed-out, composing or not-yet-completed evaluations. Closing does not defer a history write until an unfinished evaluation later returns. Clear history does not clear the current query.
- Recall restores text and flags together as a new query from the current reading row/beginning, not the historical cursor. Choosing an entry closes the popover and focuses Find. Escape/outside-click dismissal returns focus to the clock button. Clear history leaves a useful empty state.
- One Escape dismisses one eligible top layer: popover/transient, then Find, then inspection; preserve the existing Profiles/confirmation and host ownership rules. Closing/clearing Find never navigates host history. A vanished opener falls back locally without anchoring a row or requesting scroll.

### Asynchronous acceptance and reveal protocol

Use logical input identity equivalent to:

```ts
type EvaluationKey = {
  viewerEpoch: number;
  targetEpoch: number;
  instanceEpoch: number;
  windowRevision: number;
  messageRevision: number;
  queryRevision: number; // exact text and all matching modes
};
// RecordRef is an opaque context-qualified occurrence reference, never a row index.
type SelectionIntent = { id: number; key: EvaluationKey; origin: RecordRef | 'beginning' | 'end' };
type RevealIntent = { id: number; key: EvaluationKey; selectionIntentId: number; ref: RecordRef };
```

Names and representation may change during implementation; these independent validity dimensions must not disappear. The execution mechanism, cancellation implementation, Unicode/range semantics and measured numerical budgets belong to [Choose Find matching semantics and resource budgets](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/36). This decision introduces no arbitrary timing constant.

1. An evaluation can publish counts/matching data only if its complete input key still equals the live key. Reject older-query, older-window/message, older-target and older-instance results, including errors.
2. Origin, inspection, focus and user-scroll changes do not inherently invalidate otherwise current matching data. They invalidate the affected selection/reveal intent separately. Thus a current result may update counts after dismissal without restoring an origin, reopening inspection or choosing a new result.
3. An existing active reference may remain only if it survives and matches current results. An obsolete intent cannot promote a saved candidate or choose a replacement active result. A matching-data result never creates a reading anchor or inspector.
4. An intent may update the active result only while its identity and input key remain live. Maintenance evaluation has no selection/reveal intent. Navigation is disabled while pending, empty, invalid, timed out or without hits; do not queue a hidden navigation for later.
5. A viewport reveal requires a still-live reveal ID, input/context key, matching occurrence, visible eligible log view and current geometry. Resolve the occurrence to its current row only at execution. If geometry changed, remeasure the same live target; never reuse a saved numeric index or revive a canceled intent. Do not animate travel.
6. Replacing the query or context cancels obsolete evaluation work through the eventual execution contract as well as rejecting stale returns. Dismissing inspection may retain the current matching request because its counts remain useful. Clearing, hiding Find, entering Profiles and manual scrolling invalidate the relevant pending reveal immediately.
7. Matching/count updates never set following or Pause. Explicit result reveal uses the normal viewport behavior; ordinary bottom following may still move the viewport on refresh. Search does not fetch, pause or resume logs.

### Lifecycle signal and its limits

Expose an explicit monotonic instance epoch/reset signal from `SnapshotSession`, incremented when the selected container changes or an instance change is observed. Include it in snapshot/context publication before any replacement result is accepted. Do not infer it from the selected container's name, a transient empty window, a notice string or the private request generation, which also changes for Pause/visibility.

Preserve the existing restart detector: unequal known restart counts, or differing IDs when both are known, identify an observed boundary. Missing status/ID alone is not a restart; first-known metadata establishes a baseline. A count-only restart followed by its first known ID must not reset twice. Same-name repeated restarts each reset Find, including while paused. Preserve the session's existing Pause/manual-profile behavior; resetting Find does not override it.

The [current lifecycle implementation](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/blob/c0f73384c13a2bc0b0eb0ecfa1f48d9b0b324528/src/core/session.ts#L118-L144) detects these boundaries but exposes no instance epoch. Keep its guarded log-request behavior: stale completion cannot replace/clear a later instance's window. Pod deletion/UID replacement remains the original target's terminal/outdated view; do not silently adopt the new Pod. Cancel pending intents there, and use a fresh context when the user opens the replacement.

Metadata observations and name-addressed snapshot reads are not atomic. An unobserved restart cannot be reliably assigned to a particular returned snapshot. Explicit epochs solve observed lifecycle invalidation, not that host API limitation.

### Implementation boundaries and acceptance traces

- **Pure core:** shared occurrence mapping/reference lookup; inclusive/strict seek and wrap; query-event classification; state transitions and intent validity; history tuples. Replace inspection's independent occurrence-from-end identity at this seam.
- **Session/adapter boundary:** existing Pod status evidence plus explicit lifecycle epoch publication. Preserve request invalidation and retained-window limits.
- **Viewer/local input ownership:** dispatch explicit reading/inspection/query events; composition/pre-insertion capture; opener/focus suppression; one-layer dismissal; matching result acceptance. Never let a render effect select the first hit merely because matches changed.
- **Viewport/rendering:** consume validated occurrence-based reveals; preserve ordinary following, row geometry, selection and focus; decorate text/marks from the shared matching result. [Validate text-safe highlights, hidden matches and scrollbar marks](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/38) provides rendering evidence, not a second identity definition.

Required acceptance traces:

1. Reading row 64: `up` finds 73, refining through `upstream` stays 73; Next reaches 82; `upstreamx` then correction restores 82. Whole selected replacement begins again at 64.
2. No reading row, viewport far down: a new `payment` query finds the first retained match, independent of scroll. Initial Previous addresses the last match. No-match/one-hit/both-wrap cases have correct counts and local feedback.
3. Find at 82, deliberately choose/focus 90: keep query/count, clear active/candidate, no immediate jump; the next direction includes 90. Tab focus does not open inspection.
4. Inspect A, deliberately focus B, then close/evict A: preserve B. A hidden-match inspection action changes only inspector/representation. Deselecting/closing the anchor's own inspector clears that anchor without programmatic restoration recreating it.
5. Evaluation started before deselection/Close inspection finishes afterward: matching data may update if its key is current; no restored anchor, opened inspector, newly chosen result or old jump. Preserve an already established result only if it remains valid.
6. Query A then B, snapshot S then T, or message revision P then Q finishes out of order: accept only the complete live key. Test stale successes and failures, not only ordinary completion.
7. Manual scroll while evaluation/reveal is pending prevents that jump. Hide Find/open Profiles/return never replays it. Fresh explicit navigation can reveal again.
8. Duplicate example and zero-overlap eviction use the same mapping for inspector, reading row, Find, viewport and row identity. Identical whole windows preserve observed IDs without an unseen-addition claim.
9. Refresh retains surviving results without a search jump; a zero-hit query gaining matches waits for navigation. Profile changes retain only still-matching active results, without fetching or substituting a hit.
10. Select-all replacement sharing a prefix, partial paste, cut-to-empty, Undo/Redo and select-all IME composition follow the event rules. Enter used to commit composition does not navigate; stale composition completion cannot restore a cleared query.
11. Selected-text eligibility, unchanged existing query, preserved mode flags, seven-entry text/mode deduplication, zero-hit history commitment, skipped pending/error history, recall and one-layer Escape all behave as specified.
12. Repeated restarts of the same selected container, including while paused, reset all temporary Find state. Missing metadata and count-then-ID arrival do not spuriously reset. Old-instance matching/log completions and delayed reveals cannot affect the new instance.
13. Wrapping/resize/layout changes and dense/long records preserve occurrence identity and normal text selection; stale geometry never reveals the wrong row. Keep following and explicit Pause independent throughout.

Validation for this decision: read-only source audit and live maintainer decisions; glossary wording/whitespace check. No production reducer/controller, experiment branch, package install or UI/native check was performed. Matching budgets/engine evidence and rendering/packaged/native/cross-platform acceptance remain with their existing map tickets and handoff gates.

live.title: Define Find state, reading anchors and occurrence identity

live.body:
## Question

Scope update confirmed with the maintainer on 2026-10-26: prototype literal-only Find, with Match case and Whole words. Regular-expression matching and its `.*` mode control are out of scope. This overrides regex-specific controls and scenarios in the reviewed draft/screenshots; preserve the remaining compact layout and behavior. Use the literal matching contract from [Choose Find matching semantics and resource budgets](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/36), including the agreed non-overlapping occurrences. Do not add regex syntax, invalid-pattern, zero-width or hostile-pattern acceptance scenarios.

Which rendering and geometry approach can deliver the reviewed highlights, hidden-match actions and clickable scrollbar marks while preserving exact text, drag selection, focus and refresh behavior at the retained-window bounds?

Build a cheap disposable technical prototype from the matching contract, using prototype and, for UI work, impeccable. Keep the reviewed compact Find bar and chosen product behavior; the purpose is to compare implementation techniques and obtain a live human verdict, not redesign the product. Test long records and dense matches with bounded decoration work, Unicode offsets, wrapped/expanded rows, inline inspection, resizing, representation/profile changes, eviction, coincident marks and active-result visibility. Exact matching/counts must remain separate from any decoration limit.

Demonstrate original application-text-only and decoded-message-only hits with truthful explanations and explicit inspector actions. The existing All fields/Application text/Transport line tabs do not automatically prove that a decoded-only occurrence is displayed. Specify the relevant representation without guessing field paths from offsets or switching modes silently.

Exercise native DOM text selection and copyable text with generated labels/badges excluded, including a query edit and refresh while a selection survives. Establish who measures and invalidates actual row positions and how marks remain usable when positions coincide. Distinguish DOM/browser observations from clipboard or native-input acceptance.

Push the disposable prototype and measured/browser evidence without a PR or merge, link it from the ticket, and obtain the maintainer's live verdict before resolution. Preserve the desktop through background verification.

Related decisions and evidence: [Choose Find matching semantics and resource budgets](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/36); [Define Find state, reading anchors and occurrence identity](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/37); [Agree the Find implementation plan and acceptance gates](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/39).

## Appearance constraints from maintainer review

Preserve the existing pitch-black (`#000`) log canvas and absence of a line-number gutter. The prototype's earlier gray canvas and synthetic row counters were demo scaffolding, not proposed production changes.

The maintainer clarified “same row if possible” with a screenshot: the **hidden-match hint belongs alongside the log message**, wrapping below only when the available width requires it. This was not a request to combine the toolbar and Find bar; the mistaken prototype change has been reverted.

The hint itself is underlined and clickable: `Match in original text` opens Application text, and `Match in extracted message` opens Extracted message. Remove the redundant `Open…` wording. Keep generated hint text outside selected/copied log text and preserve the independent active Find result. This feedback does not accept the full rendering ticket.

[Corrected prototype and inline-hint browser observations](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/blob/becad33/docs/research/find-rendering.md).

## Constraints from the matching resolution

Use [Choose Find matching semantics and resource budgets](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/36#issuecomment-6429176710) as the canonical matching/protocol contract.

- Preserve exact matching-record counts, navigation, ordinals and scrollbar-record locations independently of decorations. Cap each range response at 4,096 text-match ranges, report coverage, and request visible-content ranges separately as needed. A global first-4,096 list must not make later or active visible hits inaccessible. Do not eagerly page through millions of offscreen ranges.
- Demonstrate incomplete-highlighting feedback for exceptionally dense content without contaminating selected/copied log text. Determine the actual DOM decoration budget and visible-range prioritization through this prototype; the packed-offset limit alone does not establish DOM performance. Separate decoration failure/pending state from already valid exact matching.
- Use the agreed Unicode/simple-folding, non-overlap and original-source provenance rules. Case folding must apply to the literal query without changing original whole-word neighbor categories; include U+0345 before/after hits, astral offsets and matches spanning presentation fragments. The corrected literal evidence is linked from the resolution.
- Carry the accepted 16,384 UTF-16-unit query limit, 100 ms pending feedback and 1,000 ms evaluation timeout into relevant interaction checks. Keep the source/count definition shared rather than inventing a second renderer predicate. Prototype timing is evidence, not packaged/native/cross-platform acceptance.

## Question

Prove whether the measured main-owned Node worker and utility-process candidates can be loaded and owned through the actual pinned Freelens 1.10.3 extension loader and extension-scoped IPC in a fully isolated host. This is an AFK prerequisite experiment, not a production implementation or the final execution/budget decision.

The [measurement evidence](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/blob/eee6f96737f8e44e3efaf16baeccb547a522df2c/docs/research/find-evaluation-measurements.md) establishes that renderer Node workers are rejected and Blob/file Web Workers fail in the installed cluster frame. Its positive main/IPC timings use an isolated app with the same Electron binary; they do not establish a loaded Freelens main extension or SDK bridge. Do not present those observations as packaged Freelens feasibility.

Use a small disposable extension artifact and a separate host profile, session/config directories and extension directory; preserve the production installation and its settings. Load the artifact through the actual Freelens loader, resolve its embedded trusted worker program or standalone child entry independently of the host working directory, and use the pinned SDK's IPC rather than a new generic remote-evaluation bridge. Exercise both main-owned candidates where feasible; record exact loading/API failures instead of silently replacing the host or weakening its CSP.

Establish the minimal request/result/cancel ownership contract: real sender/viewer context, revision correspondence compatible with [Define Find state, reading anchors and occurrence identity](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/37#issuecomment-6408002921), bounded concurrent execution, and rejection of obsolete results. Probe representative retained-window payloads plus invalid, stuck-scan and constructor-heavy patterns; measure the additional bridge/loading/termination costs. Demonstrate recovery and actual resource disposal on view/context disposal, extension disable/removal and isolated app shutdown. No production Find reducer, UI or regex policy is required.

Follow the parent map's standing instructions and docs/agents/ui-verification.md. Keep any real host window silently on workspace 7 and preserve the user's focus, workspace and pointer throughout; no attended/native-input check is authorized. Do not install the probe into the user's production host, change its preferences/CSP, replace its extension, or mutate Kubernetes resources. If a prerequisite cannot be exercised without attended input, record precisely what is deferred.

Resolve by linking the pushed disposable harness/artifact and immutable evidence, recording which candidates actually work through Freelens and which lifecycle/integration gates remain. Push a separate evidence branch without a PR or merge. Do not choose the engine, dialect or numeric production budgets here; those remain with [Choose Find matching semantics and resource budgets](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/36).

Related evidence: [Measure Find evaluation at retained-window limits](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/35); [Establish packaged Find execution and Unicode matching facts](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/issues/34).

Both candidates work through the actual pinned Freelens 1.10.3 main-extension loader and extension-scoped SDK RPC, including a real cluster-frame viewer. Renderer uses the pinned SDK invoke/handle seam, not a new remote-main-evaluation bridge; CSP and production installation remain unchanged.

The final checks use a headless labwc display with a separate installed-Hyprland instance inside it, keeping Freelens on that private session's workspace 7. All mutating display operations target the private runtime/socket. Production implementation, final input/output/cancellation budgets, full failure/long-term resource hardening, rendered UI/geometry, attended native input and Windows/macOS acceptance remain explicit downstream gates. ## What to build

Establish evidence for the integrated production package in Freelens, including real resource and lifecycle behavior, physical input/selection and the Windows/macOS contract. Publish a clear acceptance matrix whose unperformed or failing checks remain explicit release gates.

Follow the [accepted literal Find implementation and acceptance plan](https://github.com/maksimgurenko/freelens-json-logs/blob/d02b7e7c19c8e48b1cde714f0a23813b40374824/docs/design/find-implementation-plan.md). ## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Verify the actual integrated packed extension in pinned Freelens 1.10.3 and record package identity, runtime, environment and reproducible evidence. Cover all in-scope D01-D16 cases, the 13 state traces and the handoff's additional matching/execution/rendering regressions; link each to its evidence layer and verdict.
- [ ] Background host checks use workspace 7 and preserve the user's focus, workspace and pointer throughout, following current repository UI-verification guidance. Observe actual production Custom Highlights, source/geometry, snapshot/profile/restart state, following/Pause and SDK ownership. Never manufacture background focus or claim a restored desktop was uninterrupted.
- [ ] Exercise root/cluster frames sharing webContents, foreign tokens, removed frames, same-frame owner replacement, startup/idle/active cancellation, inactivity, viewer close, disable/uninstall, reactivation and shutdown. Verify actual worker exit and complete owner/listener/timer/observer cleanup.
- [ ] Run installed-host active/idle lifecycle soaks at both retention bounds, recording warm baselines and retained RAM/disk/thread/listener growth plus actual stop-to-exit behavior. Separate startup, IPC, worker, DOM and input responsiveness observations; keep sample limits explicit and remove only owned test data/processes.
- [ ] Arrange a fresh explicitly attended check or separate graphical session for physical selection/copy/clipboard, native editing/paste/Undo/Redo/IME/AltGraph, modifier shortcuts, menus, focus and window lifecycle. Earlier attended approval does not carry forward, and background DOM checks cannot substitute for physical-input evidence.
- [ ] Perform or explicitly mark unverified the corresponding Windows and macOS matching/worker/package, primary-modifier, IME, selection/copy, focus and lifecycle checks. Linux/prototype results cannot be relabelled as platform coverage.
- [ ] Record passed, failed and unperformed checks separately, with evidence and resulting release limits. Failed/unperformed production gates remain visible and cannot be treated as release acceptance. If implementation evidence invalidates an accepted mechanism or behavior, raise a precise planning question rather than silently changing the contract or substituting a fallback.
